facts.claim: 'don't want u to die' was released as a single on 3 July 2024 by Fire Records.
Deezer credits Thala as writer and Thala and George Glew as composers of the song. The track runs 3:08.
Thala is a Berlin-based singer/songwriter. The single followed her EPs In Theory Depression and twotwentytwo.
Thala said the song recalls a very dark place she once gravitated towards. She described submerging yourself in vices to avoid feeling your own pain until that becomes a coping mechanism.
Thala said that when she wrote the song, she realised it had become an anthem for anyone who needs to hear that they are great, loved and never truly alone.
Fire Records describes the song as an uplifting parable of modern-day melancholy. It calls it a cathartic pop cut with a ticking rhythm and an enormous chorus.
Fire Records says the song moves away from the 'sweet indie rock' of her earlier EPs and begins a more mature dialogue. It calls the single an introduction to her then-upcoming album.
BBC Radio 1's Sian Eleri (Future Artists) called the song 'a real teenage dream vibe'.
The song was later included on Thala's debut full-length album Avalanche, released 14 February 2025 on Fire Records. It is track 3.

Her earlier releases include the debut album Adolescence (2021), the EPs In Theory Depression and twotwentytwo (2023), and the 2024 singles '1st of the year' and 'tongue-tied & starry-eyed' (feat. Sfven).

research.lineage: Fire Records describes Thala as drawn to early-90s shoegaze, making widescreen, cinematic, off-kilter pop that it compares to Hope Sandoval trading lines with Soccer Mommy.

draft:
The first line of **don't want u to die** isn't a comfort. It's a scolding: "You have a head, why don't you use it?" Thala opens the way a worn-out friend talks at the end of a long night, impatient and close to mean. The verse lists the damage plainly. You keep getting hurt, you know it's wrong, and you won't say so. Then comes the line that sets the song's center: "But you're too nice to admit that you're not fine." It's half accusation and half tenderness. Being too nice is the flaw she can't forgive and also the thing she loves.

The chorus turns on one small word. "But I don't want you to die" follows straight on from the scolding, so the anger and the fear arrive in the same breath. Neither one cancels the other. The second verse gets harder still. The friend chooses to be alone, and the narrator says, coldly, that it's no surprise. A moment later comes "one in a million, sad you can't see it." Frustration and devotion sit side by side the whole way through, and the chorus line that hurts most is the quiet one in the middle: "I feel like I don't know you anymore." That's grief for someone who is still here.

Thala, a Berlin-based songwriter, has said the song recalls a dark place she once gravitated towards, where vices numb your own pain until numbing becomes the habit. That makes the "you" slippery. It might be a friend, or it might be a younger self she's finally yelling at. She also said that as she wrote it, it became an anthem for anyone who needs to hear they're loved and never truly alone. The lyric holds both readings.

The sound helps. A drum machine keeps a steady four-on-the-floor pulse with a prominent snare. A simple synth bass and sustained synth-pad chords hold the floor. The production is clean and dry, the voice close-miked. It's clear and mid-range, direct, at times nearly spoken, with harmonies stacked in unison to thicken it. Fire Records has compared her to early-90s shoegaze and to Hope Sandoval trading lines with Soccer Mommy. The haze of that tradition is mostly gone here. The label calls this a step away from the sweet indie rock of her EPs. What's left is a bright dance-pop frame with nothing between the singer and the listener. The song repeats its opening verse before the last chorus, the same complaint said again because it didn't land the first time.

The beat keeps you dancing while the words plead with someone who won't listen, and that mismatch lets you carry real fear without being crushed by it.
